meta.title: iTE Documentation
meta.description: Interactive Terminal Environment - AI coding agent for your terminal

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
iTE is an AI coding agent for your terminal. Connect your model service and start coding.

iTE runs as a chat interface in your terminal. You prompt, it responds, and together you build software. It can read files, run commands, search code, and edit files—safely, with your approval.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.content:
- Python 3.11+
- macOS, Linux, or Windows
- OpenAI-compatible model provider (local or cloud)

iTE uses pipx for installation to keep it isolated from your system Python.

sections.title: Configure Your Provider
sections.content:
Run `/setup` inside iTE to configure your model provider:

- Base URL: Your OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- API Key: Your provider key
- Model: The exact model name

Supported providers: Ollama (local), OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible APIs.

providers.name: Ollama
providers.note: Local models, no API key needed for basic setup

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.note: Access to many models via single endpoint

sections.title: Initialize Your Project
sections.content:
Use `/init` to analyze your project and create an AGENTS.md file. iTE reads AGENTS.md for instructions on how to work with your codebase.

The `/init` command spawns an init_investigator subagent that:
- Scans project structure (max 10 turns, 3 minute timeout)
- Detects architecture and tech stack
- Identifies build/test commands
- Extracts code style patterns
- Maps entry points

Results are synthesized into AGENTS.md documentation.

AGENTS.md supports scope hierarchy: nested files override parent instructions, allowing different rules for different parts of your project.

sections.title: Usage
sections.content:
**Configuration commands:**
/setup — Configure model provider
/config — View current configuration
/model <name> — Change model
/approval <mode> — Set approval mode (on_request, on_failure, auto, auto_edit, yolo)
/approval help — Show all approval modes
/stats — Show token usage statistics
/tools — List available tools
/theme — Change UI theme

**Session commands:**
/new — Start new conversation
/sessions — List saved conversations
/rename <name> — Rename conversation
/compact — Compact conversation history
/exit, /quit — Close iTE
/close — Close current thread

**Git commands:**
/branch — List or switch branches
/branch <name> — Switch to branch
/branch --create <name> — Create new branch
/history — Show file change history
/undo — Revert last changes
/redo — Reapply reverted changes

**Project commands:**
/init — Create AGENTS.md
/skills — Manage skills (list, show, use, add, trust)
/mcp — Manage MCP servers (start, stop, env, add, doctor)

**Subagent commands:**
/subagent list — List subagents
/subagent create — Create custom subagent
/subagent delete <name> — Delete subagent
/list — Alias for /subagent list

**Cloud commands:**
/cloud status — Show cloud auth
/cloud login — Log in to iTE Cloud
/cloud logout — Log out
/usage — Show usage summary
/activity — Show recent activity

**Memory:**
/memory — Inspect memory and controls
/memory prompt <query> — Debug prompt memory

keyFeatures.title: Ask
keyFeatures.description: Ask about code, architecture, or how things work. iTE searches and explains.

keyFeatures.title: Plan Mode
keyFeatures.description: Use /plan on to enter planning mode. iTE asks questions and produces a plan before implementing. Type /plan off to execute.

keyFeatures.title: Undo/Redo
keyFeatures.description: Type /undo to revert file changes from the last turn. /redo to reapply.

keyFeatures.title: Sessions
keyFeatures.description: Conversations auto-save. Use /sessions to resume previous conversations.

sections.title: AGENTS.md
sections.content:
AGENTS.md files provide project-specific instructions to iTE. They work like README files but for AI agents.

- Place in any directory—the scope covers that directory and all subdirectories
- Multiple files: deeper files override parent instructions
- Create with `/init` or manually

Typical contents:
- Coding conventions
- Architecture overview
- Testing approach
- Tool preferences
sections.example:
# My Project

## Architecture
- Python/FastAPI backend in src/api/
- React frontend in src/web/

## Guidelines
- Use pytest for tests
- Prefer specialized tools (read_json, edit_toml) for structured files
- Run tests after implementing changes

sections.title: Skills
sections.content:
Skills are instruction bundles that shape iTE's behavior. Install from git repos, GitHub, or local directories.

iTE supports interoperable skills from .agents/skills, .codex/skills, .cursor/skills, and other common locations.

Trust model:
- Global skills (~/.config/ite/skills) are trusted by default
- Project skills (.agents/skills) require `/skills trust` to activate

sections.title: MCP Servers
sections.content:
iTE supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for extended capabilities—databases, APIs, custom tools.

Configure MCP servers in .ite/config.toml, then connect with /mcp.

iTE includes built-in tools for reading, writing, searching, executing, and managing your codebase.

**Read tools**: read_file, read_json, read_toml, read_yaml, read_env, read_pdf, read_image, list_dir, glob, grep

**Write tools**: write_file, edit, apply_patch, edit_json, edit_toml, edit_yaml, write_env

**Execute tools**: shell, shell_start, shell_poll, shell_send, shell_stop

**Meta tools**: todos, memory, plan_question, skills

**Git tools**: git_status, git_diff, git_log, git_branch, git_commit, git_push, git_remote

**Web tools**: web_search, web_fetch, http_request

**Verification tools**: run_tests, run_linter, run_typecheck

**Subagent tools**: spawn_subagent, spawn_subagents, wait_subagent, list_subagents, cancel_subagent

Tools are categorized by risk level (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) and access type (read, write). Use /tools to see all available tools.
sections.title: Tools

sections.content:
Subagents are specialized AI agents that handle specific tasks independently. They run in parallel and return structured results to the main agent.

**Built-in subagents:**
- security_auditor — Security vulnerability analysis
- code_reviewer — Code quality review
- codebase_investigator — Explore code structure and patterns
- tooling_guardian — Validate tool configurations
- verification_reviewer — Regression-focused change validation
- init_investigator — Generate AGENTS.md for projects

**Commands:**
/spawn_subagent subagent="name" goal="task"
/spawn_subagents requests=[{subagent: "name", goal: "task"}, ...]
/wait_subagent run_ids=["..."]
/subagent list — List available subagents
/subagent create — Create custom subagent
/subagent delete <name> — Delete a subagent

Custom subagents are saved to .ite/subagents/<name>.toml
